incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 9-29 (incorporation), s. 104 (registered office), s. 106 (officers); Companies Regulation, R.Q. c S-31.1 r. 1
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) with Declaration of Registered Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital is imposed. Shares may be issued for any consideration acceptable to the board; no escrow account or paid-up capital deposit is required by Quebec law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the corporation accept the initial subscribers' share allocations, allot and issue Common Shares in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation, and record entry in the shareholders register; (2) That the registered office be established effective immediately at [Registered Address], Quebec, where corporate records and the seal shall be maintained; (3) That the following persons be appointed officers of the corporation with powers and duties under the by-laws: [President], [Secretary], and [Treasurer]; and (4) That officers be authorized to open bank accounts, sign all transaction documents, and complete regulatory filings required for the corporation to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Name Reservation Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed corporate name through the REQ online portal; identify conflicts and approval conditions; reserve the selected name for 60 days, and keep the reservation number for incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Completed Corporate Name Search Request Form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or any confusion is found, resubmit an amended name request with written justification or adopt a new distinctive name; the reservation may be pursued under s. 13 QBCA without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Filing Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign the Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) using the validated NUANS reservation, include the authorized share structure and director limitation provisions, pay the filing fee by electronic funds transfer or credit card, and e-submit the document for immediate ministerial scrutiny.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a compliance query, correct the asserted defect or provide clarifications within 10 business days; a request for expedited filing may be filed for an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec – Online Business Registration / Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, register the enterprise number with Revenu Québec through the online portal, open a GST/HST account, register for QST, and request a payroll account if staff will be hired; coordinate the federal business number via the CRA corporate registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registration is rejected due to incomplete identity information, refile corrected filings and, if tax accounts are late, submit a good-faith penalty rectification request to Revenu Québec or the CRA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene First Board Meeting and Adopt By-laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the initial board meeting under QBCA s. 107 to adopt by-laws, elect officers, approve share consideration, authorize the issue of share certificates, open board minutes, and authorize the physical establishment of the registered office in Quebec.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum is not established or a director objects to a by-law, reconvene with adequate notice or amend the by-law; shareholder ratification may be sought at a special meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration of Registered Office and Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after incorporation, electronically file the mandatory Declaration of Registered Office and Any Change of Directors or Officers, specifying the exact municipal address of the head office and the names, residential addresses, and consents of all directors; pay any registration charge if not included in the original filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried, promptly correct the given address or director details and refile; a late filing surcharge may be imposed but a voluntary compliance application will cure the failure.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Sector-based registration applicable; commercial office and data-management CRO activities are exempt from a full environmental impact assessment; physical laboratory or biosafety facilities would require an additional baseline study registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Quebec Water Quality Criteria and applicable municipal sewer by-laws; any chemical or clinical waste must be handled and disposed under the Regulation respecting hazardous materials and wastes (c. Q-2, r. 32). Ventilation discharge in office operations must not exceed applicable VOC occupational exposure limits under CNESST standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Quebec Fire Safety Régie and compliance with the Quebec Construction Code for structural load and occupancy; occupational safety and health clearance from the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST). All physical premises must obtain municipal police and fire department approval before employment begins.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online service and My Business Account portal, for federal business numbers, corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and non-resident tax accounts; Revenu Québec, including the clicSÉQUR and online services portals, for Québec corporate income tax, Québec Sales Tax (QST), employer accounts, and the Québec enterprise number (NEQ). Corporations incorporated in Québec must also comply with the Québec enterprise registry administered by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the Québec Business Corporations Act, or register the foreign corporation extra-provincially in Québec. 2. Obtain the federal Business Number (BN) and applicable CRA program accounts through CRA Business Registration Online, Form RC1, or the applicable non-resident registration procedure. The relevant accounts may include RC corporate income tax, RT GST/HST, RP payroll, and non-resident withholding accounts. 3. Obtain a Québec enterprise number (NEQ) through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec where required. 4. Register for Québec corporate income tax with Revenu Québec and file Form CO-17 where the corporation carries on business or is otherwise taxable in Québec. 5. Register for QST where the corporation is required to collect QST. 6. Register for GST where the corporation is not a small supplier or elects voluntary registration. 7. A non-resident corporation does not automatically receive a Canadian tax number merely by having foreign ownership; it must establish a Canadian filing, registration, withholding, or taxable-supply requirement. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada generally files a T2 corporation income tax return even if it claims treaty protection. 8. Maintain separate federal BN, CRA program accounts, Québec NEQ, and Revenu Québec account identifiers; the NEQ is not a substitute for the federal BN or a GST/QST registration number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian corporations are generally subject to entity-level federal and provincial corporate income taxation. Canada has no general United States-style check-the-box election for Canadian corporations. A corporation may qualify for preferential Canadian-controlled private corporation treatment, subject to statutory ownership and other conditions, but this is not a pass-through election. Partnerships and certain joint ventures may be fiscally transparent under Canadian rules, but a corporation cannot elect to be treated as a partnership merely by filing an administrative classification form. Unlimited liability corporations may have limited treaty and foreign tax classification relevance, but they remain Canadian corporations under Canadian law. Québec corporate tax treatment generally follows the corporation's legal form and statutory residence and does not provide a general hybrid-mismatch election. Hybrid mismatch arrangements may be restricted under Canada's anti-hybrid rules, including rules addressing hybrid instruments and hybrid entities, and must be analyzed separately from entity registration.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) at the federal level and Québec Sales Tax (QST) at the Québec level. Québec generally administers QST and, under the GST-QST framework, administers specified federal GST compliance functions in Québec. The combined ordinary consumption-tax burden is generally 14.975%, consisting of 5% GST and 9.975% QST, subject to zero-rating, exemptions, place-of-supply rules, and special regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, calculated under the small-supplier rules, generally measured over the relevant single-quarter and preceding four-quarter periods. QST: generally CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies under Québec small-supplier rules. Registration may be required below the threshold for specific non-resident, taxi, specified-listing, or other statutory circumstances, and voluntary registration is generally available. The CAD 30,000 threshold does not eliminate corporate income tax, payroll, withholding, or Québec enterprise-registration obligations. The 9.975% QST threshold and collection rules must be confirmed against the taxpayer's exact supply, customer, and Québec nexus profile.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Québec do not generally require universal real-time electronic invoice clearance, continuous transaction controls, or government digital stamping for ordinary private-sector CRO services. Tax invoices must contain prescribed information, including supplier identity and registration numbers where applicable, date, consideration, tax amounts or applicable tax treatment, and sufficient description of the supply. GST/HST and QST registrants generally file electronically where required by applicable filing rules and may use CRA and Revenu Québec online portals. Electronic records are acceptable if they preserve reliability, integrity, accessibility, and auditability. Electronic invoicing may be contractually required by public-sector or multinational customers, but it is not a general tax-clearance requirement. Zero-rated invoices should state the applicable statutory basis or otherwise clearly identify that tax is charged at 0%.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada are generally zero-rated for GST and, where applicable, QST if the statutory export conditions and documentary requirements are satisfied. Services supplied to a non-resident may qualify for zero-rating under the applicable GST/HST and QST export-of-services provisions where the recipient is a qualifying non-resident and the service is not excluded by a place-of-supply or use-and-enjoyment rule. For a CRO, service-by-service analysis is required. Clinical-trial management, data management, monitoring, regulatory coordination, and related consulting services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is foreign or payment is received from abroad. The analysis should address the recipient's residence and GST/QST registration status, where the services are performed and used, whether the services relate to tangible personal property, real property, or individuals in Canada, whether the services constitute testing or processing of goods that are exported, and whether a specific statutory exclusion applies. Services performed in Canada for clinical participants, services directly connected with Canadian real property, and services relating to goods remaining in Canada may be taxable or otherwise excluded from zero-rating. Export zero-rating generally permits recovery of eligible GST/QST input tax credits or refunds, subject to registration, documentation, attribution, and limitation rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For exported goods: Canadian export declaration or applicable CBSA export reporting record, commercial invoice, packing list, carrier or freight-forwarder documentation, bill of lading or air waybill, proof of export or delivery outside Canada, and records identifying the purchaser, goods, value, and export date.

For zero-rated services: executed customer agreement or statement of work, customer legal name and foreign address, evidence of non-resident status, evidence of the customer's GST/QST registration status where relevant, detailed invoices, work orders, service-delivery records, project and personnel records, evidence of offshore use or benefit where relevant, and records supporting any statutory export-of-services category.

For CRO clinical-trial services: trial protocol and scope allocation, site and investigator-location records, participant-location analysis, monitoring and data-management records, regulatory correspondence, deliverable acceptance records, and documentation distinguishing Canadian clinical-site activities from services supplied to and used by a foreign principal.

A bill of lading, customs export declaration, or inward remittance certificate is not universally required for exported services. Inward remittance evidence may support commercial substantiation but is not, by itself, a statutory condition for service zero-rating. Customs documentation is relevant to goods and to services involving exported goods.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated to Canada within 180 days, and no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applies to ordinary CRO export services. CRA or Revenu Québec may reassess tax where zero-rating is unsupported, including assessment of uncollected GST or QST, interest, and applicable gross-negligence or other statutory penalties. Input tax credits or indirect-tax refunds may be denied or clawed back where invoices, recipient status, export evidence, use-and-enjoyment analysis, or business-purpose records are inadequate. False statements, deliberate concealment, or fabricated documentation may trigger civil penalties, gross-negligence penalties, prosecution, and other enforcement measures. Directors may face personal liability in specified circumstances for unremitted amounts. The general limitation period may be extended where there is misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful blindness, or fraud. Customs misdeclarations may separately result in duties, administrative monetary penalties, seizure, interest, and prosecution under applicable customs legislation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible with no membership in the IMF's Article XIV transitional regime. There are no restrictions on capital account transactions, dividend repatriation, or profit remittance. Foreign-owned corporations may freely direct funds to non-resident shareholders, subject only to tax treaty documentation and FATF-aligned reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory requirement for export proceeds to be surrendered to the central bank or converted into CAD. Exporters may hold foreign currency in Canadian or offshore accounts without mandatory timelines or conversion ratios.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Canada does not issue dedicated e-money institution (EMI) licenses equivalent to the EU regime. Online-only banks and payment fintechs must be authorized under the Bank Act or registered as money service businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC. Foreign EMIs can only provide cross-border treasury services through a Canadian chartered bank partnership or an MSB registration, and may not offer deposit insurance or full corporate banking privileges.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of a Quebec business corporation must generally undergo an in-person KYC interview at the bank branch or with an accredited officer. Most of the six major banks permit remote onboarding through a secure video interview provided that certified true copies of corporate certificates, director passports, and beneficial ownership declarations are couriered in compliance with FINTRAC. Physical presence is mandatorily waived only for publicly listed or highly regulated entities; a privately held CRO must expect a physical or hybrid meeting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Derivative or offshore holding structure where any UBO holds citizenship or tax residency in a high-risk FATF jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an exhaustive corporate ownership chart with passport copies, provincial registry abstracts from the Registraire des entreprises, a composite source-of-funds letter from the ultimate parent, and audited financial statements demonstrating clinical trial contract expenditures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Flow of clinical trial milestone payments from multiple foreign sponsors or CRO clients, triggering potential proceeds-of-crime doubts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply executed clinical trial agreements (CTA/CPO), master service agreements, invoices from the Quebec entity, and bank references from the sponsor s parent bank. Demonstrate a clear nexus between funds received and clinical trial milestones with a documented operational ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a non-resident parent without clear Canadian investment purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File an official federal incorporation certificate, the Quebec investissement declaration, a board resolution authorizing share issuance, and a formal capital account statement from the parent company. Attach the bank's notification of direct investment to the Bank of Canada, if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident parent companies should route equity or shareholder loan through a SWIFT MT103 wire to the Quebec entity's operational account. The message must state 'Share Capital Contribution under Quebec Business Corporations Act' and include the QBCA registration number. Under Canada's no-exchange-control regime, no Bank of Canada approval is needed; however, FINTRAC may require an electronic fund report if the transfer exceeds CAD 10,000. For foreign direct investment, the bank may request Form B2 – Report of Foreign Direct Investment under the Canada Business Corporations Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade settlements are executed primarily via SWIFT MT103 for sub-CAD 1M milestone payments. For high-value protocol logistics or large drug-sample vendibles, a commercial letter of credit under UCP600 can be issued through a tier-1 Canadian bank. Domestic CAD settlement occurs via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the new Real-Time Rail (RTR) for instant payments, while USD payments clear through the US Federal Reserve wire system via US correspondent banks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for counterparty jurisdictions with non-convertible currencies, such as certain emerging-market clinical sites)
Cross-currency swaps (fixed/floating against CAD with no underlying physical transaction)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the enterprise registration date in the REQ register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory interest and late-filing penalty; non-filing for two consecutive years triggers a notice of intent to dissolve and administrative strike-off from the REQ register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporation Income Tax Return (T2) with financial statements and applicable T-schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance-due day is 2 months (CCPC) or 3 months (non-CCPC) after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); repeated default within 3 years raises base to 10%; daily prescribed interest and possible prosecution for wilful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (CO-17) and schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance due 2 months (CCPC) or 3 months (other) after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); daily prescribed interest; fault-based penalties for gross negligence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal (CBCA) Annual Return; applicable only where the corporation is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 200 late-filing fine; arrears exceeding one year entitle the Director to initiate dissolution (CBCA s.212).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll information returns: federal T4 Summary and Quebec Relevé 1 (RL-1) slips plus summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (T4) and Revenu Québec (RL-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following each calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: T4 late filing penalty of CAD 25/day (min CAD 100, max CAD 2,500) plus CAD 100 per omitted slip; Quebec imposes an equivalent daily penalty for late RL-1 filings with interest.
